draft.title: Electrolysis
card: Electrolysis uses an external power supply to force a non-spontaneous redox reaction to happen. The cell converts electrical energy into chemical energy.

In an electrolytic cell the anode is positive and the cathode is negative. Oxidation happens at the anode and reduction happens at the cathode. Electrons are pushed from the anode to the cathode through the external circuit.
In a molten salt, only the two ions are present. The cation is reduced at the cathode and the anion is oxidised at the anode. Molten sodium chloride gives sodium metal and chlorine gas.

In an aqueous solution, water can also react. At the cathode, the strongest oxidising agent present is reduced. At the anode, the strongest reducing agent present is oxidised. Use the electrochemical series to compare them.
draft.remember: Electrolysis forces a non-spontaneous reaction: oxidation at the anode, reduction at the cathode.

a.q: What is the role of the external power supply in an electrolytic cell?
opts: It forces a non-spontaneous redox reaction to occur
It speeds up a reaction that is already spontaneous
It stores the chemical energy released by the reaction
It allows ions to move through a salt bridge
a.why: The reaction would not happen by itself, so electrical energy must be supplied to drive it. Speeding up a spontaneous reaction is the job of a catalyst, not a power supply.
a.clue: Think about whether the reaction would run without it.

b.q: Molten potassium bromide, KBr, is electrolysed using inert electrodes. What forms at the anode?
opts: Bromine, from oxidation of bromide ions
Potassium, from reduction of potassium ions
b.why: A molten salt has no water, so only K⁺ and Br⁻ are present. Anions are oxidised at the anode, so bromide ions form bromine. Potassium would form at the cathode, not the anode.
b.clue: Which ions are in the molten salt, and which electrode attracts anions?

a.best: It forces a non-spontaneous redox reaction to occur

b.best: Bromine, from oxidation of bromide ions
